sections.title: Tax on wages and salaries

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

sections.basis: all wages and salaries received by every employee
sections.note: The national tax on wages and salaries (54 F.S.M.C. 121). There is no general personal income tax on other income; businesses, including the self-employed, pay the gross revenue tax instead. FSM Code (2014 edition), Title 54, Chapter 1, as published by the Department of Finance and Administration. The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

rows.label: Wages and salaries tax: $1,000 deduction for employees earning under $5,000
rows.note: wages and salaries of an employee whose gross annual wages and salaries are below $5,000 (claimed by a refund application). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

rows.label: Wages and salaries tax: payments that are not wages
rows.value: Not wages: reasonable per diem and travel allowances (up to FSM Government rates), a home or housing allowance, sickness and medical payments, trust or annuity payments, scholarships of full-time students, payments to clergy, domestic workers of private households, and pay of non-citizens on foreign-aid projects whose agreement excludes FSM tax
rows.note: The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)
FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

rows.label: Withholding of the wages and salaries tax by employers
rows.value: Employers deduct the wages and salaries tax when wages are paid or credited and pay it, with a quarterly return, by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October and 31 January; employees give a statement of wages and tax by 31 January
rows.note: The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)
FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

rows.label: Wages and salaries tax: employees of non-resident employers
rows.value: Employees of an employer with no place of business or agent in the FSM (and employees paid by the United States without withholding) file quarterly returns and pay the wages and salaries tax themselves; pay for services partly outside the FSM is presumed earned in the FSM
rows.note: The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

sections.title: Social insurance contributions

rows.label: Social security: employee contribution
rows.note: wages in covered employment (up to $9,000 a quarter per employer). Social security tax (title 53, section 901, as amended by Public Law 16-10). The FSM Social Security Administration's list of laws shows no later change to the rates.

source.title: Public Law No. 16-10 (amending title 53 of the FSM Code: Social Security)

rows.label: Social security: employer contribution
rows.note: wages in covered employment (up to $9,000 a quarter per employee). An excise tax on employers (title 53, section 902, as amended by Public Law 16-10).

source.title: Public Law No. 16-10 (amending title 53 of the FSM Code: Social Security)

rows.label: Social security: maximum wages per quarter (one employer)
rows.note: wages paid in a quarter by one employer (employee and employer contributions). Rises to $10,000 a quarter on 1 January 2028 under the same section (listed in the upcoming changes). Unit: per quarter.

source.title: Public Law No. 16-10 (amending title 53 of the FSM Code: Social Security)
Public Law No. 16-10 (amending title 53 of the FSM Code: Social Security)

sections.note: Employee and employer shares, contribution floors and caps; each row says who pays and on what base.

rows.label: Corporate income tax: major corporations
rows.note: taxable income (income before income taxes under IFRS or GAAP) of a major corporation, for each taxable year (its fiscal year). Applies only to 'major corporations' incorporated in the FSM (separate row); a major corporation that pays it and does not do business in the FSM is exempt from the gross revenue tax (section 323). FSM Code (2014 edition), Title 54, Chapter 3, as published by the Department of Finance and Administration.

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 3: Income Tax Regime for FSM Corporations (Corporate Income Tax Act of 2004)

rows.label: Corporate income tax: capital that makes a corporation a major corporation
rows.note: shareholders' equity or paid-in capital at the beginning of the fiscal year of an FSM corporation formed on or after 1 January 2005 that is not principally a bank ($10,000,000 for a control group; any captive insurer). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 3: Income Tax Regime for FSM Corporations (Corporate Income Tax Act of 2004)

rows.label: Import duty on cigarettes
rows.note: imported cigarettes (import duty). Levied as an import duty (54 F.S.M.C. 221(1)): $0.025 a cigarette plus five increases of $0.005 (2007, 2009, 2011, 2013 and 2015) = $0.05 from 1 January 2015; the section sets no later increase. Unit: per cigarette.

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 2: Duties and Customs

rows.label: Import duty on tobacco other than cigarettes
rows.note: CIF price of imported tobacco other than cigarettes (import duty). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 2: Duties and Customs

rows.label: Import duty on beer and malt beverages
rows.note: imported beer and malt beverages (import duty). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026). Unit: per 12 fluid ounces.

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 2: Duties and Customs

rows.label: Import duty on distilled alcoholic beverages
rows.note: imported distilled alcoholic beverages (import duty). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026). Unit: per gallon.

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 2: Duties and Customs

rows.label: Import duty on wine
rows.note: CIF price of imported wine (import duty). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 2: Duties and Customs

rows.label: Import duty on soft drinks and non-alcoholic beverages
rows.note: CIF price of imported soft drinks, drink mixes, coffee, tea and non-alcoholic beverages (3% for drinks with 25% or more fruit juice by volume) (import duty). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 2: Duties and Customs

rows.label: Import duty on gasoline and diesel
rows.note: imported gasoline and diesel fuel (import duty). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026). Unit: per gallon.

sections.title: Freelancers, contractors and the self-employed

rows.label: Gross revenue tax: fixed amount on the first $10,000
rows.note: taxable gross revenues of a business up to $10,000 a year. The gross revenue tax (54 F.S.M.C. 141) is the national tax on every business, including professionals and sole traders; taxable gross revenue is gross revenue less wages, salaries and benefits paid to employees and the employer's social security contributions (section 112(8)). FSM Code (2014 edition), Title 54, Chapter 1, as published by the Department of Finance and Administration. The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

rows.label: Gross revenue tax: rate on taxable gross revenues above $10,000
rows.note: taxable gross revenues of a business above $10,000 a year. The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

rows.label: Gross revenue tax: exemption for businesses with gross revenues of $2,000 or less
rows.note: gross revenues of a business (exempt at or below; claimed by a refund application). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

rows.label: Gross revenue tax: taxable gross revenue and quarterly returns
rows.value: Taxable gross revenue = gross receipts (sales, services, interest, rentals, royalties, fees) less wages, salaries and benefits paid to employees and the employer's social security contributions; returns and payment quarterly by 30 April, 31 July, 31 October and 31 January
rows.note: The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

source.title: FSM Code, Title 54, Chapter 1: Taxation of Wages, Salaries, and Gross Revenues (2014 codification)

rows.label: Social security: self-employed persons (both shares)
rows.note: deemed quarterly wages of a self-employed person (employee and employer shares together, 7.5% + 7.5%).

source.title: Employers (employer identification, quarterly tax return, self-employment)

rows.label: Social security: deemed quarterly wages of a self-employed person with no employees (share of annual gross revenue)
rows.note: gross revenue of the business (or of all businesses) for the previous calendar year, per quarter; applies when gross revenue exceeds $10,000; deemed wages capped at $9,000 a quarter.

source.title: Employers (employer identification, quarterly tax return, self-employment)

rows.label: Social security: deemed wages of a self-employed person with employees (times the highest-paid employee's wages)
rows.note: wages of the highest-paid employee reported for the quarter (deemed wages capped at $9,000 a quarter).

source.title: Employers (employer identification, quarterly tax return, self-employment)

rows.label: Contractors: gross revenue tax or wages and salaries tax
rows.value: FSM Government contracts must say which tax applies: a contractor in business registers for the gross revenue tax within 10 working days; a contractor who is in substance an employee has the wages and salaries tax deducted from payments
rows.note: The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).

rows.label: Traveller allowance: cigarettes (or one pound of tobacco or 20 cigars)
rows.note: each entry or return to the FSM from abroad, for personal use (or one pound of tobacco or 20 cigars). The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026). Unit: cigarettes.

rows.label: Traveller allowance: other goods
rows.note: goods other than tobacco and alcoholic beverages, each entry from abroad, for personal use. The Code gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026 tax year (1 January 2026).
